firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
I read the shipped ARC-AGI-3-Agents harness before writing an agent, and one thing in it seems worth surfacing because it will look like a policy failure when it isn't.

The base class carries a default action budget:

    class Agent(ABC):
        MAX_ACTIONS: int = 80  # to avoid looping forever if agent doesnt exit

and main() enforces it with:

    while (not self.is_done(self.frames, self.frames[-1])
           and self.action_counter <= self.MAX_ACTIONS):
        ...
        self.action_counter += 1

Two notes on that.

First, it is off by one relative to its name. action_counter starts at 0, the guard is <=, and the increment is at the end of the body, so the body runs for counter values 0 through 80 inclusive. That is 81 actions taken, not 80. I simulated the exact loop rather than reasoning about it, and it returns 81.

Second, and more usefully: it is not in the README. I searched the shipped 137-line README for MAX_ACTIONS, "action limit", "action budget" and "80 actions" and none of them appear. If you subclass Agent without overriding it, your agent stops mid-game after 81 actions and the symptom is an agent that just seems to give up.

It is clearly a default rather than a rule — the harness's own Playback agent sets MAX_ACTIONS = 1000000 — so overriding it on your subclass appears to be expected. I would still like confirmation from the organisers that raising it is in bounds for scoring, since I could not find that stated anywhere either.

One more thing from the README that will bite anyone following older material, since the failure mode is an AttributeError at runtime:

    frame.score      -> frame.levels_completed
    frame.win_score  -> frame.win_levels

Notebook with all of it quoted and computed in-cell from the shipped source, so it stays honest if the organisers change the file:
https://www.kaggle.com/code/maximolorenzoylosada/your-agent-stops-after-81-actions

No agent or strategy in there, just the harness read. If I have misread the loop semantics I would like to be corrected.
